Theory of More Efficient Propulsion Method by Soviet engineer V. Shabetnik

#ufotwitter

Propulsion system would use high-temperature superconductors, electrical currents, and magnetic effects to produce thrust — potentially enabling highly efficient movement in space.

The concept challenges conventional propulsion methods by converting electrical and internal energy directly into thrust rather than expelling mass (like rockets do).

Shabetnik imagines a Spherical spacecraft covered in superconductive material, with internal electron accelerators creating currents that interact to produce force.

New Theoretical Basis

Particle Structure and Superconductivity

Shabetnik suggests subatomic particles (like electrons) have specific structures in ways not accounted for in mainstream quantum physics — a speculative premise to justify new mechanisms.

From this, he develops a non-standard view of superconductivity with potential implications for energy conversion.

He proposes that high-temperature superconductors eliminate electrical losses and thus are key to new devices.

Overview of the Spacecraft Design

The craft would be spherical and completely coated with high-temperature superconducting material.

Inside, at least three high-velocity electron accelerators would be mounted and able to move along the spacecraft’s equator.

Power would come from either a nuclear reactor or Shabetnik’s proposed generator with claimed internal energy amplification.

Mechanism of Thrust

The accelerators emit streams of high-velocity electrons that travel along the superconducting hull, inducing currents in the hull.

Interaction between the emitted electron flow and the induced currents produces an “ampere force” — in essence, a magnetic force perpendicular to the electron movement.

This interaction, Shabetnik claims, generates thrust without expelling mass — a departure from Newton’s third law in conventional propulsion.

Flight Control and Acceleration

By controlling electron current magnitude and direction, the craft could adjust flight direction and speed.

Shabetnik suggests that if acceleration equal to Earth’s gravity were possible, this craft could near relativistic speeds in under a year.

Conclusions and Future Potential

The published report concludes that principles proposed by Shabetnik appear correct to researchers involved.

It suggests refining components, discovering new superconductors, and eventually designing a prototype spacecraft (~5 m diameter).

If successful, the technology might also apply to earthbound transport like cars or aircraft — claiming ecological benefits.

The article also mentions that experimental models showed movements resembling “flying saucers”, fueling speculative interest.

You really should read this because another Russian engineer, Ivan Filimonenko, claims that in 1957, while working for the military, he built an electromagnetic disc-shaped vehicle.
